title: Deprogramming corporatism: why big-company habits kill founders and early hires
summary: Garry Tan explains how big-corporate culture (busywork without results, cover-your-ass politics, buzzword-following) trains people in habits that fail in startups. The fix is relentless focus on concrete results, building product and talking to customers, and a founder culture reinforced by the people around you.

principles.text: In a startup you can't just look busy; you must actually make a product people want, because there is no air cover.
principles.quote: There’s no air cover for startups. You don’t have backup troops. It’s just you versus the world. So naturally, if your product or service sucks, then you die.

principles.text: Be wary of hiring big-company directors and managers; they often fail fast in startups, to everyone's surprise.
principles.quote: often they’ll try to grow the team by hiring experienced directors and managers from corporations that are well known and successful. Many of them fail pretty quickly, and it’s always a surprise to everyone, especially the experienced hire.

principles.text: Founders and CEOs must keep the team focused on what matters, not on covering themselves or taking credit.
principles.quote: Startups can sometimes develop a cover-your-ass culture too, but that’s the job of the founders and CEO to keep people focused on things that actually matter.

principles.text: Don't follow buzzwords or trends; you have to be right about the future and make life better for specific paying customers.
principles.quote: Startups can’t survive blindly following buzzwords or whatever trend is hot because you actually have to know what’s coming in the future and be right.

principles.text: Work on things you know are right that most people don't yet know; ask what valuable company nobody is building.
principles.quote: It turns out you have to work on things that a) you know are right, and b) most people don’t know yet.

principles.text: The antidote to corporate habits is results: build product, talk to customers, and think in concrete numbers.
principles.quote: We spend a lot of time trying to get founders to focus on action and results — build product, talk to customers, that’s it. Think in terms of concrete numbers
